# The XOR check works as follows:
# - Starting edx = 0xffffffbd (which as a signed 32-bit is -67, but we use lowest byte: 0xbd)
# - For each position i from 0 to 26 (27 characters total):
#   - input[i] XOR (edx & 0xff) must equal target[i]
#   - Then edx += input[i]
# 
# To invert: input[i] = target[i] XOR (edx & 0xff)
# Then update edx += input[i]

target = bytes([
    0xfb, 0x4f, 0x0e, 0xd7, 0xac, 0x3f, 0xda, 0x56, 
    0xff, 0x9b, 0x0a, 0xad, 0x43, 0xc4, 0x90, 0x11,
    0xb7, 0x2e, 0xc0, 0x45, 0xf7, 0xa8, 0x67, 0xb5,
    0x80, 0xc3, 0x5e
])

length = 27  # 0x1b

edx = 0xffffffbd  # Initial value

result = []
for i in range(length):
    # Get the low byte of edx for XOR
    key_byte = edx & 0xff
    # input[i] XOR key_byte = target[i]
    # So input[i] = target[i] XOR key_byte
    input_byte = target[i] ^ key_byte
    result.append(input_byte)
    # Update edx by adding input[i]
    edx = (edx + input_byte) & 0xffffffff

recovered = bytes(result)
print("Recovered input:", recovered)
print("As string:", recovered.decode('latin-1'))

# Verify the solution by running the forward check
print("\n--- Verification ---")
edx = 0xffffffbd
for i in range(length):
    key_byte = edx & 0xff
    xor_result = recovered[i] ^ key_byte
    expected = target[i]
    match = "OK" if xor_result == expected else "FAIL"
    print(f"i={i}: input={chr(recovered[i]) if 32<=recovered[i]<127 else '?'} ({recovered[i]:02x}) XOR {key_byte:02x} = {xor_result:02x}, expected {expected:02x} [{match}]")
